$comment: Single source of truth for the playground: every app listed here exists in apps/<id>/ and is built and shown in the gallery.
`id` is immutable: it is the folder name under apps/, the URL segment, and the key used to derive the GitHub and CLI links.
Build output is assumed to be 'dist'; add "outDir" only when the toolchain differs (e.g. Next.js static export writes to 'out').

apps.name: Starter
apps.description: The smallest setup that still shows what Morphic Blocks is made of: elements, modes and views, with one mount call and five short behaviors.
apps.details:
Each of the five blocks (print, text, number, math and repeat) has five elements: a title, an icon, a one sentence hint, pseudocode and JavaScript. Three modes pick from these elements, one per view: toolbox tiles show title, icon, block and hint; the workspace shows plain word pseudocode; the code view shows JavaScript and is editable by structure.

A small ⓘ button next to each pane names the mode it shows. Run executes the program and shows what it printed. Copy this app to start your own project.

apps.name: Embed Anywhere
apps.description: A friendly tutorial article about loops with three small block editors placed between its paragraphs, each one the same reusable web component with a live Python preview and a Run button.
apps.details:
The page reads like an ordinary blog post. Between the paragraphs sit three figures, one per step: repeat a fixed number of times, count with a variable, and repeat while a condition holds. Each figure has its own tray of blocks, a workspace, a live Python preview and a small output area. It opens with a starter program whose output is already shown, and Run refreshes the output after the reader changes the blocks.

All three are the same <morphic-editor> custom element, built with Lit and configured only by attributes: which blocks its toolbox offers, which program it starts with, its height and its caption. Each instance runs its own Morphic Blocks engine, so the editors stay fully independent, and the tag could be dropped into a CMS, a wiki or a learning platform just like an image. Behaviors turn the blocks into JavaScript with the same meaning as the Python shown, and a loop that never ends is stopped after a thousand rounds.
